chief_complaint: sudden intermittent bouts of screaming and drawing legs to chest with passage of currant-jelly stool (Intussusception)
hpi_details: 8-month-old male infant brought to ED with 12 hours of sudden-onset, severe, paroxysmal episodes of crying and irritability where the baby screams inconsolably, draws his knees up to his abdomen, and turns pale. Episodes last 3-5 minutes, after which the baby appears exhausted and lethargic. Two hours ago, mother changed his diaper and discovered dark red, gelatinous, mucus-mixed stool.
ideas: mother terrified watching baby scream in agony and pass bloody jelly-like diapers
concerns: mother worried baby has a ruptured intestine or internal hemorrhage
expectations: wants immediate pain medicine and emergency abdominal ultrasound or X-ray
pmh: Had a mild upper respiratory adenovirus infection 1 week ago

clinical_knowledge.topic: Acute ileocolic intussusception evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Acute ileocolic intussusception is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes STAT pediatric surgical notification, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: sudden intermittent bouts of screaming and drawing legs to chest with passage of currant-jelly stool (Intussusception)

Key HPI features: 8-month-old male infant brought to ED with 12 hours of sudden-onset, severe, paroxysmal episodes of crying and irritability where the baby screams inconsolably, draws his knees up to his abdomen, and turns pale. Episodes last 3-5 minutes, after which the baby appears exhausted and lethargic. Two hours ago, mother changed his diaper and discovered dark red, gelatinous, mucus-mixed stool.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 155, BP 88/54, RR 34, Temp 37.4C. Infant appears lethargic between pain spasms with episodic pallor. Abdominal palpation reveals a firm, sausage-shaped mass in the right upper quadrant/epigastrium, with corresponding emptiness in the right lower quadrant (Dance sign positive). Rectal exam reveals gross blood and mucus mixed resembling currant jelly on glove. Abdominal ultrasound confirms a large, multi-layered concentric ring / bull's-eye target sign in the transverse colon representing telescoping of the terminal ileum into the cecum and ascending colon (ileocolic intussusception).
Relevant background/PMH: Had a mild upper respiratory adenovirus infection 1 week ago
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Acute ileocolic intussusception.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Gastroenteritis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Currant jelly stools.
management_principles: After establishing IV hydration and verifying absence of peritonitis or free air on radiographs (no perforation), proceed immediately to fluoroscopically or ultrasound-guided Pneumatic (Air) or Hydrostatic (Saline) Enema Reduction under sedation by pediatric radiology/surgery
Air enema successfully reduces 80-90% of ileocolic intussusceptions
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 8-month-old male presenting with episodic colicky abdominal pain (drawing legs up) and currant-jelly stools following a recent adenovirus infection.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: HR 155, BP 88/54, RR 34, Temp 37.4C. Infant appears lethargic between pain spasms with episodic pallor. Abdominal palpation reveals a firm, sausage-shaped mass in the right upper quadrant/epigastrium, with corresponding emptiness in the right lower quadrant (Dance sign positive). Rectal exam reveals gross blood and mucus mixed resembling currant jelly on glove. Abdominal ultrasound confirms a large, multi-layered concentric ring / bull's-eye target sign in the transverse colon representing telescoping of the terminal ileum into the cecum and ascending colon (ileocolic intussusception).
reference_soap.assessment: Acute Ileocolic Intussusception with Currant Jelly Stools and lethargy.
reference_soap.plan: STAT pediatric surgical notification. After establishing IV hydration and verifying absence of peritonitis or free air on radiographs (no perforation), proceed immediately to fluoroscopically or ultrasound-guided Pneumatic (Air) or Hydrostatic (Saline) Enema Reduction by pediatric radiology/surgery. Air enema successfully reduces 80-90% of ileocolic intussusceptions. If enema reduction fails after 3 attempts, or if peritonitis/perforation occurs, transfer to operating room for laparoscopic/open manual surgical reduction and bowel viability assessment.

learning_objectives: Recognize the classic clinical triad of pediatric intussusception (episodic colicky pain with knee-to-chest posturing, vomiting, and bloody currant jelly stools)
Palpate for the characteristic right upper quadrant sausage-shaped abdominal mass combined with right lower quadrant emptiness (Dance sign)
Identify the pathognomonic ultrasound 'target sign' / 'pseudokidney sign' of invaginated bowel segments
Compare non-operative Pneumatic/Air Enema reduction vs surgical manual reduction indications and techniques

teaching.one_liner: 8-month-old boy with episodic screaming, knees drawn to chest, lethargy between episodes, and currant-jelly stools.

must_ask.say: Does he scream and pull his knees up in episodes, then seem okay in between?
Can you describe the stool you found — what color and consistency?
How does he act between the crying episodes — playful or very tired?
Has he had a cold or virus in the past couple of weeks?
We'll likely try a special enema using air or fluid guided by ultrasound to un-telescope the bowel, which works most of the time without surgery.
